prs.title: feat(oxfmt)!: format `parser:markdown` files by `oxc_formatter_markdown`
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Part of #24607

Now oxfmt formats Markdown files natively with `oxc_formatter_markdown`.

Basically the same output with Prettier 3.9.9, but we already covers some not yet released fixes as well. Please see DIVERGENCES.md.

Before, Markdown files were formatted by Prettier. So, JS in Markdown code fence was also formatted by Prettier (babel/typescript).

But now it is handled by `oxc_formatter`, it means `sortImports` and `sortTailwindcss` works.

For Markdown code fence langauge detection, we uses shiki languages (https://shiki.style/languages).

We also supports `::: directive` syntax, both VitePress (`::: withspace`) and remark-directive (`:::withoutspace`). (BLOCK only, no LEAF and TEXT position)

prs.title: perf(formatter_markdown): pre-allocate the IR buffer
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Measured on 19,487 real-world Markdown files (mdn content, oxc-ecosystem-ci repos):

- IR elements / source bytes: median 0.29, p95 0.40, p98 0.46
- `0.4x` alone covers 94.9% of files without reallocation
  - With the 1024 floor, 97.6% (small documents have a higher ratio)
- `0.5x` would reach 99.5%, but over-allocates 96% of the used size instead of 66%

prs.title: fix(lexer): context walk line break and type end rules
prs.author: ShanonJackson
prs.body:
- != at the start of a line continues the expression and as or satisfies there ends it, as tsc does; a type that ends a line goes on with an initializer or a body, and on one line a type ends at any token that cannot continue it (x as T - 1, c ? x as T : y)
- simplifies the walk steps and anchors a walk at a function or class only where a declaration starts, disambiguate is 380 code lines shorter
- every valid input whose tokens change now matches tsc, main set neutral

prs.title: refactor(lexer): answer dense context questions with the full walk
prs.author: ShanonJackson
prs.body:
- a bounded walk starts fresh at its anchor for every question and keeps nothing between questions, once the bounded walks of a pass have taken as many scan steps as the full walk would the full walk answers the rest
- drops walk continuation, group leaving and the separator and angle jumps, disambiguate is 247 code lines shorter; also fixes a template in tsx type arguments being lexed as an unterminated JSX element
- main set about 1% slower, mostly code layout (checker.js runs the same instruction count), ts_zod about 5% slower since its class body questions walk the members again

fix(oxlint,oxfmt): set stderr blocking
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Closes #27361

We already set blocking mode for stdout/stdin, but not for stderr.

### Repro

1000 files with a parse error (`const a = ;`), so stderr exceeds 64KB.
The reader waits 3s before reading, so the pipe fills up:

```sh
node dist/cli.js --check . > out.txt 2> >(sleep 3; cat > err.txt)
```

| | exit | stderr | errors shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| stderr to a file (baseline) | 2 | 90739B | 1000/1000 |
| Before | 2 | 65536B | 723/1000 |
| After | 2 | 90739B | 1000/1000 |

Before this fix, the output stops at exactly 64KB, and the final `Error occurred when checking code style...` line is missing too.

And by bumping `oxc-toml`, TOML 1.1 syntax is supported.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): one entry for bounded context walks
prs.author: ShanonJackson
prs.body:
- before, after and the open angle count go through one bounded walk entry, and after starts the scan past the token it is asked about so the scan jumps a closer's group itself
- drops the scan's angle count, the anchor position check and an always true jump check, none of them changes an answer; disambiguate is 60 code lines shorter
- no token changes on any input, main set neutral, adversarial about 2% faster

prs.title: refactor(packages/codegen): rename `CAT_OP_LT_THEN_UN_NOT`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Pure refactor.

Rename `CAT_OP_UN_NOT_AFTER_LT` to `CAT_OP_LT_THEN_UN_NOT`. The old name was confusing - it could read as "not after LT" whereas what it really means is an operator "unary not" _is_ after LT. Rename it to remove this confusion.

prs.title: fix(packages/codegen): fix debug assert fail printing `TSJSDocNonNullableType`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
When printing `<` followed by `!` in a TS type e.g. `Array<!T>`, the `last` category recorded is `CAT_OP_UN_NOT` instead of `CAT_OP_LT_THEN_UN_NOT`, which is the more usual category to record for `<!`.

In this case, `CAT_OP_UN_NOT` is fine. The purpose of `CAT_OP_LT_THEN_UN_NOT` is to insert a space before printing `--`, which would form an HTML-style comment `
